newsitem.title: UK: LCE robusta ends firm but off highs in thin range.
newsitem.headline: LCE robusta ends firm but off highs in thin range.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended firm on Monday but below highs after trading a narrow $15 a tonne range dominated by an active front-month switch, traders said.
At the close on Monday the benchmark November contract was up $11 at $1,545 but below a session high of $1,556.
Volume on the exchange reached 3,512 lots.

Traders said prices should remain supported by New York's arabica contract, buoyed by news of possible delays in Colombian coffee exports due to trucker protests, crumbling infrastructure and leftists guerrilla attacks.
"And while force majeure has not been declared yet, there are no signs military activity will die down in the short-term," broker GNI said on Monday.
Traders said much of the action on Monday focused on the September/November switch where the premium soared to a high of $101 a tonne before settling at $49 at the close.
"There has been good industry buying," said one trader.
Traders said options-related buying was also prevalent after some 394 lots of January call options at stirkes of $1,600 and $1,650 were traded.
Trade also included some 212 lots of November put options at strikes of $1,500 and $1,600 a tonne.
Robusta values took a beating last week after touching a high of $1,740 on August 27 following a buildup in US speculative long positions and forecasts for higher supply in the 1996/97 season.
Chartists on Monday said the contract faces steep resistance at $1,580 a tonne with a slide expected if it is not breached.
"My feeling is it's going to head down towards the key support of $1,450," said Richard Gardiner, technical analyst at Gerald Ltd.
